title: Press archive
manifesto: Not a news ticker — an outside audit. Each entry is on-the-record journalism documenting facts in the Lagovsky case.

items.title: Awaiting extradition: the Justice Minister holds the last word
items.summary: RFE reports that for almost six months the final extradition decision has remained with Justice Minister Nenad Vuić, who has no statutory deadline. In the meantime Lagovsky says he lost his work permit and health coverage, and the family is living in prolonged uncertainty.
items.focus: The article links the ministerial deadlock to the pending asylum and constitutional proceedings, and records the defence position that Serbia must not extradite where Article 3 ECHR risks remain unresolved.

items.title: Appeal court wouldn't touch the defence — only Moscow's bundle
items.summary: N1 presents the defence claim that the Serbian courts checked only the formal extradition file from Moscow and did not engage with the substance of the innocence evidence, including Russian arbitration rulings on the underlying transaction.
items.focus: The piece records the argument that there is no properly demonstrated reasonable suspicion and that the courts refused to weigh the defence material on the merits.

items.title: Belgrade family caught between deportation and the draft
items.summary: Nova focuses on the family impact: two sons integrated into Serbian schools, Lagovsky out of work, and the extradition file already passed to the minister after the appeal stage.
items.focus: It also highlights the asylum request as a live legal obstacle that requires Serbia to examine risk before any surrender takes place.

items.title: Serbia one ministerial signature away from extradition
items.summary: RFE records that after the appeal ruling of 3 December 2025, the last domestic decision-maker on extradition became the Serbian Justice Minister, whose act is administrative rather than judicial.
items.focus: The report captures the defence warning that ministers rarely reverse an extradition once the courts have approved it, which makes the ministerial stage decisive in practice.

press_call.title: For journalists
press_call.text: Arbitration, extradition, asylum, Interpol — primary documents and defence filings are open. Ask for anything.
press_call.thesis: Serbia isn't extraditing a fugitive. It's extraditing a lawyer who drafted a lawful contract. If that stands, international law is just paperwork.
